ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the value of d: it is the only method on the path that splits d into its raw bits, and the special-value decision belongs with that split. Hops 1-4 never inspect d (hops 1-3 pass their arguments on; hop 4 tests only the scale factor, returning d for a zero scale factor, and converts any other scale factor into the increment of the exponent bits). Once the exponent bits of an infinite or NaN value have been incremented, the carry has overwritten the sign bit and the exponent field is zero, so the returned -0.0 (or negative subnormal) cannot be told apart from the scaling of an ordinary value and no caller can recover infinity or NaN from it. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('If d is 0 or NaN or Infinite, it is returned unchanged'); MathUtils.nextAfter returns NaN or infinite d unchanged directly before it splits the double in raw components (MathUtilsTest testNextAfterSpecialCases); MathUtils.round returns infinite values unchanged and NaN as NaN (MathUtilsTest testRoundDouble, testRoundFloat). No caller can make the gold's own arithmetic give the special values back: the variant gold returns an infinite or NaN d only for a zero increment, a zero scale factor never reaches the gold (hop 4 returns d itself) and hop 4 is documented to pass the increment matching any non-zero scale factor; a caller that tests NaN and infinity itself re-implements the gold's decision and bypasses the gold. The gold still returns -0.0 for (+infinity, 2^52), an input every javadoc on the path admits.
